title: Glowsmith — Neon Sign Workshop
description: Bend glass by hand, fill it with argon, wire up a bad ballast, and take the whole sign home as a PNG.
concept: A full neon fabrication bench in one page. Drag to bend tube freehand, type copy that is converted into single-stroke glass paths by a hand-built vector alphabet, stamp stock shapes, then fill each tube with one of ten gases and wire it to a flicker, chase, sweep or breathe circuit. The wall behind it is procedural — brick, black board, acrylic or a night street — and the glow is a real two-layer bloom, not a CSS shadow. Signs save to a shelf in the browser, pack into a share link, and export at 2× as a PNG.
features: Five tools: freehand tube bending, type setting, shape stamping, select/move, and cutting
Ten named gas fills, adjustable bore, and six wiring modes (steady, breathe, blink, bad ballast, chase, marquee sweep)
Built-in single-stroke tube alphabet — 47 glyphs bent into real glass paths with tracking and slant
Twelve stock shapes, four procedural backings, and glow/bloom/mains-buzz controls
Undo/redo, localStorage shelf of named signs, share-link encoding, and 2× PNG export

interaction.mouse: Drag on the wall to bend a tube; drag a selected tube to reposition it.
interaction.click: Tap to stamp a shape, set type, cut a tube, or drop a glass bead.
interaction.touch: Every tool is pointer-driven and touch-tested; the panel becomes a bottom sheet.
interaction.keyboard: D/T/S/M/E switch tools, Z and Y undo and redo, Delete removes the selection, Esc deselects.
